messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: rstan traceplot ignores inc_warmup?
parts:
Using the development code, with r5 created by combining 3 parallel runs
of 2,000 iterations each,
> traceplot(r5, "lp__")
> traceplot(r5, "lp__", inc_warmup=FALSE)
get me the same plot as far as I can tell, except that the background
for first 1,000 iterations are shaded gray in the first version and not
in the second.

I tried traceplot(r5, pars="lp__", inc_warmup=FALSE), but that was the
same as the second version.

As an aside, it might be nice to allow control over the vertical scale
or choice of iterations; the graph is completely dominated by the fact
that the starting values were terrible: it is essentially a vertical
line going up and horizontal line going across. Some way to zoom in
would be nice.

Work-around:
> x <- extract(r5, "lp__", permuted=FALSE, inc_warmup=TRUE)
> dim(x)
[1] 2000 3 1
> plot(x[50:2000, 1, 1])
> plot(x[50:2000, 2, 1])
> plot(x[50:2000, 3, 1])

Substantively the graphs seem to indicate convergence, even from the
50th iteration on--a nice improvement on my earlier model.

Ross

parts:
On 9/19/13 12:49 PM, Ross Boylan wrote:
> Using the development code, with r5 created by combining 3 parallel runs
> of 2,000 iterations each,
>> traceplot(r5, "lp__")
>> traceplot(r5, "lp__", inc_warmup=FALSE)
> get me the same plot as far as I can tell, except that the background
> for first 1,000 iterations are shaded gray in the first version and not
> in the second.

If that's the case, and "inc_warmup" is the right name, then
it's a bug. Removing warmup should give you only the part
that wasn't grey in the first half.

> I tried traceplot(r5, pars="lp__", inc_warmup=FALSE), but that was the
> same as the second version.
>
> As an aside, it might be nice to allow control over the vertical scale
> or choice of iterations; the graph is completely dominated by the fact
> that the starting values were terrible: it is essentially a vertical
> line going up and horizontal line going across. Some way to zoom in
> would be nice.

Vertical scale as in log vs. linear? Or something that
would truncate the values outside of a fixed range? I don't
know how that works in R graphics.

> Work-around:
>> x <- extract(r5, "lp__", permuted=FALSE, inc_warmup=TRUE)
>> dim(x)
> [1] 2000 3 1
>> plot(x[50:2000, 1, 1])
>> plot(x[50:2000, 2, 1])
>> plot(x[50:2000, 3, 1])
>
> Substantively the graphs seem to indicate convergence, even from the
> 50th iteration on--a nice improvement on my earlier model.
